# Proxy images used by the scenarios, pinned so that a red run is unambiguous:
# with httpd:latest / nginx:latest a failure could be a Vaadin regression or a
# proxy upgrade, and there is no way to tell them apart after the fact.
#
# Two whitespace-separated columns: the proxy tree, then its pinned image.
# The tree column lets a per-proxy run ship only the image it will actually
# load — an Apache-only run has no use for nginx, traefik and haproxy, and
# every test job paid for them twice, once downloading the tarball and once in
# `docker load`. A full sweep (no tree selected) still ships all of them.
#
# The build job pulls these once and ships them in the same tarball as the app
# image, so no scenario job ever touches Docker Hub. Anonymous pulls are
# rate-limited per source IP and GitHub-hosted runners share egress, so that
# was a live flake source as well as a cost.
#
# Compose files reference them as ${HTTPD_IMAGE:-...} / ${NGINX_IMAGE:-...},
# so a one-off sweep against a different proxy build needs no file edits:
#   HTTPD_IMAGE=httpd:2.4.67 docker compose up
#
# Keep in sync with the defaults in the compose files. Dependabot's
# docker-compose ecosystem bumps those; this list has to follow.
apache-httpd    httpd:2.4.68
nginx           nginx:1.31.6
traefik         traefik:v3.7
haproxy         haproxy:3.2.23
